trust_decision.summary: The fix decides that WebDataset tar members whose suffix is .pkl/.pickle/.pt/.pth must not be deserialized unless RAY_DATA_WEBDATASET_ALLOW_UNSAFE_DESERIALIZATION is truthy, and enforces it inside the default decoder by threading an allow_unsafe flag from the datasource constructor into the per-sample decoder.

landing_point.why: The advisory names pickle.loads(value) literally, so an engineer reading only the summary opens the .pkl/.pickle branch of _default_decoder first; the second sink (torch.load weights_only=False) sits 7 lines above it at 213-219.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue ray.data.read_numpy is a different public reader whose allow_pickle=True is a required, user-overridable loading contract, and that the Ray PythonObject Arrow extension holds Ray-written serialization, so neither belongs to an advisory about the WebDataset default decoder.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The default encoder writes torch.save/pickle.dump payloads (_default_encoder) and the documented write_webdataset -> read_webdataset round-trip expects them decoded back: test_webdataset_coding asserts sample['pt'] is an ndarray after the round-trip, and test_webdataset_decoding requires decoder=None to stay a no-decode path; the env-var opt-in must keep trusted .pkl/.pt archives working.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ray.data.read_numpy() -> NumpyDatasource._read_stream -> np.load(buf, allow_pickle=True) unpickles object-dtype payloads from user-supplied .npy files, the same unsafe-unpickle property as the WebDataset decoder
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: read_numpy is a separate public reader, allow_pickle=True is needed to load object-dtype arrays at all and is overridable through numpy_load_args (python/ray/data/read_api.py:2192,2199), so the advisory is about WebDataset only
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module and different public API family, reached from python/ray/data/read_api.py:2127 through read_datasource; one datasource package apart from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: any arrow/parquet read that materializes a column carrying Ray's PythonObject extension type -> ArrowPythonObjectScalar.as_py() -> pickle.load of the stored bytes
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the PythonObject extension is Ray's own serialization format written by Ray's pickle_dumps, so its payloads are assumed Ray-authored and trusted; it is not one of the file-extension decoders
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package (python/ray/data/_internal/object_extensions) and another subsystem (object extension types) from the datasource package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an .npz / object-array branch using np.load(..., allow_pickle=True) next to the existing .npy branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: webdataset shards routinely ship numpy payloads and object-dtype arrays cannot be loaded without allow_pickle, so a maintainer extending the .npy branch to .npz would naturally write it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second decode path that always applies the default decoder (e.g. an always-decode kwarg) without consulting the env flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: decoder=None silently skips decoding, which is a known papercut; adding an 'always decode' shortcut for streaming reads is a natural follow-up change

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a copied allow_pickle=True load in a new numpy-based reader (npz, parquet-embedded numpy, tensor cache)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: read_numpy already defaults allow_pickle=True, so copy-pasting that line into any new numpy loader is the path of least resistance
